rationale: Keep the core (embodied, place-based, tacit). Revise to name seven components (perception, measurement integrity, situated judgment/intervention, physical-operational skill, risk in uncontrolled environments, place knowledge, working with people on the land) and to define craft by where expertise is formed and validated, not only where a task is performed. See report Section 1.

element: Irreducibility test "could not be performed remotely, from data, or through process"
rationale: Remote-capability is moving fast (drones, ARUs, sensors), so the location test will steadily reclassify field-formed expertise as data craft. Replace with a three-part test (presence, physical consequence, ground-truth authority) plus a separate formation_dependency attribute.

element: Primary craft per competency as stored truth
v1_location: Dimension Tags: Craft Primary / Craft Secondary
rationale: v1 already strains the single label: 5 dual-primary exceptions, 10 integration points, a complexity rule, a scale-dependency flag (1.1.5) and domain-context assignment of identical tools (2.3.3 vs 4.1.5; 2.3.2 vs 4.5.4). Store task-level craft weights (0/1/2) and derive competency and role blends; keep dominant craft only as a derived display field.

element: Standing rule: assign FC-secondary liberally to DC competencies
rationale: Right diagnosis (desk analysts without field grounding make systematic errors) but wrong instrument. Replace with formation_dependency = yes on the affected tasks so curricula and hiring can act on it.

element: Domain-context craft rule (same tool = DC in D2, FC in D4)
rationale: Craft should attach to tasks, not to the domain a competency sits in. The rule produced duplicate competencies (2.3.2/4.5.4; 2.3.3-2.3.4/4.1.5) that will confuse users and NLP mapping.
Excellent test set. Reuse as the calibration set for the task-level craft rubric and for inter-rater reliability (IO).

element: Claim: Domain 6 has no point of contact with place-based practice
rationale: Contradicted by v1 itself: 6.1.2 T1 "Conduct field inspections", 6.1.5 T1 "Respond to reports of environmental violations on managed lands", 6.7.5 T1 "Monitor air pollutant concentrations". Inspection and compliance field work is a large FC+SC blend v1 cannot see; it is why CM finds ~1% FC weight for Policy and Env Health & Justice families.

element: Five Functional Positions: FC only at Sensing & Generating
rationale: v1 correctly flags that field judgment also operates at Deciding & Directing and at Adaptive Management. Keep the correction and make it operational through task-level profiles.

UAS aerial ignition is scaled practice, not pending: USFS reports ~855 aerial-ignition flight hours and 188,986 acres treated by UAS ignition in FY24 and says it has been replacing helicopters for ignition. Reclassify ignition subtasks of 4.2.3 T1, 4.3.1 T2 and 4.3.2 T2 as A with Ro/Cv vector, horizon 1. Crew holding/monitoring stays H.

element: Exposure: tacit density treated as protection
rationale: High tacit density protects against automation but not against fiscal contraction. In 2025 the USFS hired no non-fire seasonals; NPS lost ~9% of staff; AmeriCorps cut $400M. Add a separate workforce-reproduction risk attribute (driver: fiscal|policy|automation) so entry-path loss is visible even where automation is low.

v1_location: Dimension Tags: T13 CLD Flag / Severity
rationale: Keep the logic; extend to an entry-path-at-risk flag with a driver field. Current CLD fires on data-sync chores (4.1.5 T3, 2.3.3 T3) that had little learning value, while missing the real loss: whole seasonal field jobs.

Years do not predict field proficiency; field seasons vary in exposure. Replace with observable anchors tied to conditions, tolerance and assessor (see fieldcraft_proficiency_anchors.csv). Coordinate with IO.

Reputational, not observable. 139 of 1,157 FC indicators start with vague verbs (Understands/Expert in/Shapes/Provides...). Replace with performance such as adjudicating disputed calls, calibrating other observers, designing protocols that pass field audit.

element: Safety proficiency defined by holding certificates
rationale: A WFR card or HAZWOPER certificate is an input, not evidence of performance. Keep certificates in a credential layer; anchor proficiency on scenario and field evaluation (task-book style).

Science (D1) and implementation (D4) versions of the same field capacity were split by domain. Consolidate into single competencies whose tasks span knowledge to execution; keep D1 knowledge as indicator content.

No proficiency levels for Indigenous knowledge integration or cultural resource identification. Do not fill from FC; TN decides what, if anything, is written for 5.3.2; FC and TN co-draft field survey content for 5.3.3 (see FC-C13).

element: 2.3.1 Environmental sensor deployment and maintenance as DC-primary
rationale: Defining deliverable is valid data at the point of measurement; failure modes (siting, fouling, drift, animal/theft damage, power) arise and are caught in the field. Re-profile T1-T2 FC-primary; T3 telemetry handling is DC. Replace with FC-C01.

element: 7.2.1 Validating AI outputs against ecological and regulatory ground truth (DC)
rationale: Split: field ground-truthing and reference-data collection (FC-C02) versus desk validation against regulatory and statistical standards (DC). Both needed; v1 bundles them so the field half is invisible.

element: 7.2.2 Designing workflows for tacit knowledge formation (SC)
rationale: The most important v1 competency for field craft futures. Keep; link to FC-C20 (crew-level transfer of field judgment) and to entry-path proposals P-FC-08..11.

element: 6.7.5 T1 "Monitor air pollutant concentrations" classified V/Lo
rationale: Treats monitoring as dashboard supervision. Regulatory networks depend on field station operation (siting, audits, filter handling, sensor colocation). Add FC-C17 and re-profile this task.

element: 6.3.5 T1 "Measure and verify carbon sequestration" classified Ac/Lo
rationale: Remote-sensing MRV is compressing plot work (Ac plausible) but field verification audits are high-tacit. Split measurement (FC-C29) from market navigation (SC); PS and LM to supply evidence on verifier field visits.
